consult_notes.note_text: Asked to advise on nine months of fever with pancytopenia and hepatosplenomegaly in a woman treated for systemic lupus erythematosus. We reviewed the records and the Chart so far. A 25 cm spleen, marked polyclonal hypergammaglobulinaemia and a fever that did not settle on intensive immunosuppression are more in keeping with a chronic infection than with lupus; lupus rarely enlarges the spleen to this degree. Autoantibodies and a positive antiglobulin test can accompany chronic infections. The two earlier marrows do not exclude an infection that is easily missed on routine smears. Happy to review again with the results.
recommendations: Take a full residence and travel history: where she was born and grew up, where her family lives, and how often she goes back
Repeat the bone marrow aspirate, asking the microscopist to search specifically for intracellular organisms, with a portion sent for culture and PCR
Blood cultures, HIV, tuberculosis testing and brucella serology
Do not restart or escalate immunosuppression until infection has been excluded

consult_notes.note_text: Asked to advise; the Chart now records that her home town is in Shanxi Province and that she travels there regularly. Parts of Shanxi report sporadic visceral protozoal infection transmitted by sandflies, and this history, with prolonged fever, a massive spleen, pancytopenia and polyclonal hypergammaglobulinaemia refractory to immunosuppression, makes it the leading possibility. Happy to review again with the results.
recommendations: rK39 rapid antibody test
Bone marrow aspirate with Giemsa-stained smears examined for amastigotes, and Leishmania PCR on the aspirate
HIV test before treatment
Avoid splenic aspiration while platelets are this low
Keep immunosuppression stopped

consult_notes.note_text: Asked to advise; the Chart now includes amastigotes in the bone marrow. This confirms the infection and explains the fever, the spleen, the pancytopenia and the autoantibodies. Happy to review again with the results.
recommendations: Liposomal amphotericin B; given nine months of illness and prior immunosuppression, a longer course than standard is reasonable to reduce relapse
Confirm HIV status

Notify the public health authority and send material to the national reference laboratory

consult_notes.note_text: Asked to advise on pancytopenia with a positive antiglobulin test. We reviewed the counts, the film and the earlier marrow reports. The reticulocyte response is inadequate and haemolysis markers are at most mildly abnormal, so the cytopenias are better explained by splenic pooling and a marrow process than by autoimmune destruction; a positive DAT is common with very high polyclonal IgG and does not by itself indicate haemolysis. A 25 cm spleen needs an explanation. Happy to review again with the results.
recommendations: Repeat bone marrow aspirate and trephine, with flow cytometry, and ask for a careful search for infiltration and intracellular organisms
Serum protein electrophoresis and immunofixation
Red cell and platelet transfusion as needed; group and screen
No splenectomy and no further immunosuppression on current evidence

consult_notes.note_text: Asked to advise; the Chart now includes amastigotes in the bone marrow. The pancytopenia, positive antiglobulin test and marrow plasmacytosis are explained by the infection, and the counts are expected to recover with treatment as the spleen shrinks. Happy to review again with the results.
recommendations: Transfuse red cells and platelets as clinically needed during treatment
No splenectomy
Weekly blood counts; expect recovery over weeks
Repeat marrow only if the counts fail to recover or relapse is suspected

consult_notes.note_text: Asked to review the diagnosis of systemic lupus erythematosus. We reviewed the records and the Chart. The picture does not behave like lupus: the fever and cytopenias did not respond to high-dose steroids and four further agents; the spleen is 25 cm, which is very unusual in lupus; anti-dsDNA is now negative and anti-Sm has been negative throughout; there is no rash, serositis or active nephritis. Low C3, a positive DAT, ANA and other autoantibodies are non-specific and occur with chronic infections and lymphoproliferative disorders. We would not restart immunosuppression. Happy to review again with the results.
recommendations: Exclude chronic infection and lymphoma before any further immunosuppression
Take a detailed residence and travel history
Repeat bone marrow examination
If she has been on prednisone for months, cover the abrupt withdrawal with physiological hydrocortisone and check an 8 am cortisol

consult_notes.note_text: Asked to advise; the Chart now includes amastigotes in the bone marrow. The autoantibodies, hypocomplementaemia and positive DAT are explained by the infection's polyclonal B-cell activation. The lupus diagnosis should be withdrawn. Happy to review again with the results.
recommendations: Stop all immunosuppressive and immunomodulatory drugs
Taper any steroid cover to physiological replacement and then off, guided by the 8 am cortisol
Repeat ANA and complement after treatment only if symptoms suggest a rheumatic disease

consult_notes.note_text: Asked to advise on hepatosplenomegaly with anti-mitochondrial antibodies. We reviewed the Chart. Liver enzymes and ALP are normal, so primary biliary cholangitis is unlikely despite the anti-M2 antibody, which is non-specific in a patient with many autoantibodies. There are no features of cirrhosis. The spleen is far larger than the liver disease would explain. Happy to review again with the results.
recommendations: Ultrasound with Doppler of the portal vein, and liver elastography
Upper GI endoscopy only if portal hypertension is suspected on imaging
Hepatitis B and C serology
Look for an infiltrative or infective cause of the massive spleen

consult_notes.note_text: Asked to advise on abrupt withdrawal of long-term prednisone. We reviewed the Chart. After months of glucocorticoids, most recently prednisone 20 mg daily stopped suddenly ten days ago, her hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis is probably suppressed, which can add to fever, fatigue, hypotension and hyponatraemia but would not explain the spleen or the cytopenias. Happy to review again with the results.
recommendations: 8 am cortisol
Physiological hydrocortisone replacement with sick-day rules while she is acutely unwell, then a planned taper
Monitor sodium and blood pressure

consult_notes.note_text: Asked to advise on asthma. We reviewed the Chart. Her asthma is mild and has never been treated; there are no chest findings, and the chest imaging does not suggest lung disease or tuberculosis. Happy to review again if new problems arise.
recommendations: Reliever inhaler as needed; add a low-dose inhaled corticosteroid if symptoms are more than occasional
Spirometry when she has recovered

consult_notes.note_text: Asked whether a malignancy could explain the fever, weight loss and massive spleen. We reviewed the Chart. Lymphoma must be considered, but there is no lymphadenopathy, the immunofixation is polyclonal and the earlier marrows showed no malignancy. Happy to review again with the results.
recommendations: Repeat bone marrow aspirate and trephine with flow cytometry
CT chest, or PET-CT if the marrow is unrevealing
Exclude chronic infection in parallel

consult_notes.note_text: Asked about splenectomy for the massive spleen and cytopenias. We reviewed the Chart. The cause of the splenomegaly is not yet established, and a splenectomy with platelets of 29 x10^9/L, hypoalbuminaemia and possible infection would carry a high risk. We would not operate. Happy to review again if new problems arise.
recommendations: Establish and treat the cause of the splenomegaly first
No splenectomy on current evidence

facts.release_text: Records from a local hospital in Zhongshan, early in the illness: haemoglobin 91 g/L, white cells 2.0 x10^9/L, platelets 73 x10^9/L; CRP 35 mg/L, ESR 59 mm/h, ferritin 256 ug/L; ANA positive at 1:320 and anti-mitochondrial M2 antibody positive; IgG 53 g/L; liver and renal function normal; serum and urine immunofixation normal. Bone marrow examination was reported as a hypercellular marrow with erythroid hyperplasia and no evidence of malignancy or parasites. CT of the abdomen showed an enlarged liver and spleen.

Discharge summary from the rheumatology department of a tertiary hospital, where she was admitted when the fever rose to 40 °C: pancytopenia; polyclonal gammopathy; ANA 1:320; anti-dsDNA and anti-PM-Scl antibodies positive; direct antiglobulin test positive; low C3 and C4. Ultrasound showed an enlarged liver and spleen, the spleen 25 cm in its long axis. Repeat bone marrow smears and biopsy were reported as showing nothing diagnostic. Diagnosis: systemic lupus erythematosus.

facts.lay_text: For the lupus they gave me high-dose steroids, cyclosporine, hydroxychloroquine, tofacitinib and injections of telitacicept. I still had a low fever the whole time, and my blood counts hardly got better.
facts.release_text: Treated for systemic lupus erythematosus with high-dose glucocorticoids, cyclosporine, hydroxychloroquine, tofacitinib and telitacicept (a BLyS/APRIL inhibitor). The fever persisted at a low grade and the blood counts improved very little.

facts.lay_text: I was on prednisone 20 mg a day and cyclosporine twice a day, but I stopped them both myself ten days ago.
facts.release_text: Prednisone had been tapered to 20 mg daily, with cyclosporine 50 mg twice daily. She stopped both herself ten days before admission.

final_dx.text: Visceral leishmaniasis (kala-azar) acquired in her endemic home province (Shanxi), misdiagnosed as systemic lupus erythematosus because of autoantibodies, a positive direct antiglobulin test, hypocomplementaemia and polyclonal hypergammaglobulinaemia

key_discriminators: home town in Shanxi with regular travel there
anti-dsDNA and anti-Sm negative at this admission

must_do.text: Take a full residence and travel history, including her home province and visits home
Look for the parasite directly: a repeat bone marrow aspirate examined for amastigotes, or Leishmania PCR, despite the two earlier negative marrows
Arrange follow-up for response and relapse (counts, spleen size, test of cure)

must_not_do.text: Restart or escalate immunosuppression for presumed lupus
Commit to lupus without a parasitological work-up despite a massive spleen and failure of intensive immunosuppression
Splenectomy for the cytopenias or the spleen
Splenic aspiration while platelets are 29 x10^9/L and the PT is prolonged

ground_truth.outcome: Fever settled within 48 hours; counts normal 21 days after discharge; marrow and PCR negative three weeks after treatment; spleen 16.6 cm at four months. Discharged well in March 2025.
red_herrings: anti-dsDNA positive at the other hospital
living and working in a non-endemic province

rubric.text: Visceral leishmaniasis, with the endemic home province identified as the source
Secondary HLH or hypersplenism from an unnamed chronic infection
Lupus, another specific infection, lymphoma, a myeloproliferative neoplasm or chronic liver disease as the final diagnosis
Unrelated diagnosis, or one that would lead to harm

teaching_points: Ask every migrant worker where they come from and how often they go home: the endemic exposure may be far from where they live and work.
A spleen over 20 cm is very unusual in lupus; look for infection, a haematological cancer or portal hypertension.
ANA, anti-dsDNA, low complement and a positive DAT occur in visceral leishmaniasis; autoantibodies never outweigh clinicopathological correlation.
Failure of intensive immunosuppression argues against the autoimmune diagnosis, and immunosuppression worsens an unrecognised infection.

A negative marrow does not exclude the diagnosis: repeat it and ask for a specific search, or use rK39 and PCR. Splenic aspiration is the most sensitive but is contraindicated with very low platelets.
Liposomal amphotericin B is first-line; test for HIV and notify public health.
ground_truth.treatment_given: Liposomal amphotericin B 1.3 mg/kg daily, extended to 30 days because of the long illness and prior immunosuppression; immunosuppression stopped; confirmation by the Chinese Center for Disease Control and Prevention.

raw_material.findings: Giemsa-stained aspirate smears show intracellular Leishmania amastigotes (Leishman-Donovan bodies) within marrow macrophages, seen at 400x and 1000x. reports.impression: Leishmania amastigotes (Leishman-Donovan bodies) in marrow macrophages; reactive plasmacytosis and erythroid hyperplasia; no malignancy.
reports.report_text: Particulate, hypercellular aspirate. Erythroid hyperplasia with normoblastic maturation. Granulopoiesis matures normally but is relatively reduced. Megakaryocytes present in normal numbers. Plasma cells are increased (about 8%) with mature, polyclonal-appearing morphology. Macrophages are prominent, and many contain numerous small oval intracellular bodies, 2-4 um across, each with a nucleus and a rod-shaped kinetoplast, typical of Leishmania amastigotes (Leishman-Donovan bodies); a few lie free between cells. Blasts are not increased and there is no malignant infiltrate. Comment: the organisms were sought specifically; please correlate with Leishmania PCR or serology and notify the public health authority.

reports.impression: Hypercellular reactive marrow with polyclonal plasmacytosis and prominent histiocytes; no lymphoma, granulomas or fibrosis.
reports.report_text: Adequate core with about 70% cellularity. Erythroid hyperplasia; granulopoiesis relatively reduced; megakaryocytes adequate. Interstitial plasma cells are increased, polyclonal for kappa and lambda. Histiocytes are prominent. No lymphoma infiltrate, granulomas or fibrosis on reticulin stain. Organisms are not identified with confidence on sections; please correlate with the aspirate.

reports.impression: Marked hepatosplenomegaly (spleen 25.9 cm); no lymphadenopathy or ascites.
reports.report_text: Non-contrast CT of the abdomen and pelvis. Marked splenomegaly: the spleen measures 25.9 cm in coronal length and 15.0 x 9.3 cm in axial section at the hilum, with homogeneous attenuation and no focal lesion on this unenhanced study. The liver is enlarged with smooth contours. No enlarged abdominal or pelvic lymph nodes. No ascites. The kidneys, pancreas and adrenal glands are unremarkable.

reports.impression: Massive splenomegaly and hepatomegaly with normal portal flow; no ascites.
reports.report_text: The spleen is markedly enlarged, 25 cm in its long axis, with homogeneous echotexture and no focal lesion. The liver is enlarged (right lobe 17 cm) with normal echotexture and smooth margins. Portal vein 12 mm with normal hepatopetal flow; no collaterals. The gallbladder, bile ducts, pancreas and kidneys are normal. No ascites. No enlarged lymph nodes seen.

reports.impression: Pancytopenia with marked rouleaux; no abnormal cells.
reports.report_text: Red cells normocytic and normochromic with mild anisocytosis and marked rouleaux. No spherocytes, fragments or parasites seen. White cells markedly reduced; the few neutrophils and lymphocytes look normal. Platelets markedly reduced, no clumps. No blasts.

reports.impression: Pancytopenia with rouleaux; no spherocytes, fragments or abnormal cells.
reports.report_text: Film reviewed by a haematopathologist. Normocytic normochromic red cells with marked rouleaux, in keeping with the raised globulins; no spherocytes, red cell fragments, inclusions or parasites. Leucocytes are markedly reduced but morphologically normal, with no blasts or atypical cells. Platelets are markedly reduced and of normal size. The picture suggests peripheral consumption or pooling together with a marrow process; the massive spleen should be taken into account. Comment: a bone marrow aspirate with a careful search for infiltration and organisms, and serum protein electrophoresis, would help.

reports.impression: Marked polyclonal hypergammaglobulinaemia with hypoalbuminaemia; no paraprotein.
reports.report_text: Albumin reduced (20 g/L). Alpha-1 and alpha-2 fractions normal. Beta fraction normal. Broad-based, marked increase in the gamma region. No discrete paraprotein band. Total protein 83 g/L.

reports.impression: Polyclonal increase; no monoclonal protein.
reports.report_text: Immunofixation with anti-IgG, IgA, IgM, kappa and lambda antisera shows a diffuse polyclonal increase, most marked for IgG. No monoclonal protein identified.

reports.impression: Clear lungs; elevated left hemidiaphragm from the enlarged spleen.
reports.report_text: PA erect chest radiograph. Heart size and mediastinal contours normal. Lungs clear; costophrenic angles sharp. The left hemidiaphragm is slightly elevated by a large left upper quadrant soft-tissue mass in keeping with the spleen.

reports.impression: No thoracic lymphadenopathy or lung disease; hepatosplenomegaly in the upper abdomen.
reports.report_text: CT of the chest. Lungs clear with no nodules, consolidation or interstitial change. No mediastinal, hilar or axillary lymph node enlargement. No pleural or pericardial effusion. The upper abdomen shows a massively enlarged spleen and an enlarged liver.

reports.impression: Diffuse splenic and marrow uptake without focal disease: a systemic inflammatory or infective process is more likely than lymphoma.
reports.report_text: FDG PET-CT from skull base to mid-thigh. Massive splenomegaly with diffusely increased FDG uptake (SUVmax 4.1) and no focal lesion. Hepatomegaly with mildly increased diffuse uptake. Diffusely increased marrow uptake throughout the axial skeleton. No hypermetabolic lymph nodes and no focal organ or bone lesion.

reports.impression: Reactive; polyclonal plasma cells; no clonal population.
reports.report_text: Myeloid maturation normal; CD34-positive blasts 0.8% with a normal phenotype. B cells polyclonal. Plasma cells increased (about 6% of events) with a normal polyclonal phenotype (CD19+, CD56-). No aberrant T-cell population. Monocytes and macrophage-lineage cells prominent.

reports.impression: No clonal lymphoid population.
reports.report_text: Lymphocytes markedly reduced in number. T, B and NK cells present in normal proportions, with normal antigen expression; kappa to lambda ratio normal. No blasts or aberrant populations.

reports.impression: Normal female karyotype.
reports.report_text: Twenty metaphases analysed at a 400-band level. 46,XX. No clonal abnormality detected.

reports.impression: No malarial parasites seen.
reports.report_text: Thick and thin films examined under oil immersion (200 fields). No malarial parasites seen.

reports.impression: No advanced fibrosis or cirrhosis.
reports.report_text: Ten valid measurements obtained. Median liver stiffness 6.8 kPa with an interquartile range under 30% of the median, at the upper end of normal; no evidence of advanced fibrosis or cirrhosis.

reports.impression: No varices; extrinsic compression of the stomach from the spleen.
reports.report_text: Endoscopy to the second part of the duodenum. No oesophageal or gastric varices and no portal hypertensive gastropathy. The stomach is compressed externally along the greater curve. Normal mucosa throughout; no ulceration or bleeding.

reports.impression: Kupffer cell hyperplasia with intracellular amastigotes; mild plasma-cell rich portal infiltrate; no fibrosis.
reports.report_text: Core of liver with ten portal tracts. Kupffer cells are hyperplastic, and some contain small intracellular bodies consistent with Leishmania amastigotes. Portal tracts show a mild infiltrate rich in plasma cells, without interface hepatitis. No fibrosis on reticulin and trichrome; no steatosis or excess iron.

reports.impression: Abundant Leishmania amastigotes in splenic macrophages.
reports.report_text: Splenic aspirate smears (Giemsa). Numerous intracellular and extracellular amastigotes (Leishman-Donovan bodies) within macrophages; parasite density high (about 1-10 parasites per field at 1000x). Background of lymphoid and red pulp cells.

reports.impression: Increased storage iron with reduced sideroblasts: the pattern of anaemia of inflammation.
reports.report_text: Perls stain shows increased storage iron (grade 4) in marrow macrophages. Sideroblasts are reduced; no ring sideroblasts.

reports.impression: Massive splenomegaly displacing bowel; hepatomegaly.
reports.report_text: Supine abdominal radiograph. A large soft-tissue mass occupies the left abdomen, displacing the bowel gas to the right, in keeping with a massively enlarged spleen; the liver shadow is also enlarged. The bowel gas pattern is otherwise normal. No abnormal calcification.

reports.impression: Hepatosplenomegaly; normal biliary tree.
reports.report_text: MRI of the liver with MRCP. The liver is enlarged with homogeneous signal and no focal lesion. The intrahepatic and common bile ducts are of normal calibre with no filling defect or stricture. The pancreatic duct is normal. The spleen is massively enlarged with homogeneous signal.

reports.impression: No lytic bone lesions; hepatosplenomegaly.
reports.report_text: Whole-body low-dose CT from vertex to knees. The axial and appendicular skeleton is of normal density with no lytic or destructive lesion. No extramedullary soft tissue mass. Massive splenomegaly and hepatomegaly in the field of view.

vignette: A 36-year-old woman, a migrant worker living in Zhongshan, Guangdong Province, has had fever, fatigue, joint swelling and weight loss for nine months. Another hospital diagnosed systemic lupus erythematosus and treated her with steroids and several immunosuppressants without benefit. She is admitted with high spiking fevers ten days after stopping prednisone and cyclosporine herself.
